problem: A user returning after several exchanges still had to interpret route rails, CURRENT and Git chronology manually to learn what changed and what matters.

behavior: shows up to six addressed changes since the browser's explicit local caught-up mark
prefers active/current heads without creating canonical priority
FOCUS reuses FIELD selection; OPEN enters the existing route
MARK CAUGHT UP writes only one local timestamp in this browser

laws: No backlog, queue, cloud read state or second activity feed.
No canonical file is mutated by using CATCH UP.
Route timestamps are manifest evidence, not proof that a user has read or understood a change.
Exact Git chronology remains CHANGE / GIT; CATCH UP is an orientation projection.

verification.human: Use after being away; pass if NOW + 1-6 changed heads restores orientation faster than manually opening CURRENT/ROUTES/CHANGE.

residue: Catch-up currently explains a route from evolution.mutation when available, otherwise role/transfer. It does not synthesize cross-route narrative or conversation history.
stop: Do not add notifications, server-side read tracking, another dashboard or autonomous prioritizer from this feature.
